intention: charging.manual_charge_entries is keyed on tesla_id, account_id is demoted to created_by_account_id and never read as a filter, and no manual-charge write can run without a vehicleref.Ref.
request: MAG-68 — 5. Demote charging.manual_charge_entries.account_id to created_by_account_id. Step 5 of MAG-63.

decisions.what: The three internal/analytics read ports drop accountID, so analytics reads every manual charge for a car whoever typed it.
decisions.why: It matches supercharger sessions, which RM57 already made car-wide. Manual entries were the last charging source still filtered by account.

decisions.what: Update and Delete take a vehicleref.Ref; the SQL keeps WHERE id = $1 AND tesla_id = $2.
decisions.why: Only the gateway's authorizeVehicle can build a Ref and vehicleref-guard enforces it, so a missed call site is a compile error, not a security hole. Same shape RM57 gave VerifySession.

decisions.what: The four Reader ports keep int64 rather than taking a vehicleref.Ref.
decisions.why: internal/analytics calls them and make vehicleref-guard forbids building a Ref outside the gateway. RM57 kept its read ports on int64 for the same reason.

decisions.what: Three tiers, split charging / charging / gateway, with tier 1 carrying the analytics and mechanical gateway call-site updates.
decisions.why: Mirrors RM57, which folded consumer call-site updates into the owning module's tier and gave the gateway its own tier for the real authorization work.

decisions.what: UpdateEntry and DeleteEntry keep an account predicate in tier 1, on the renamed column. Tier 2 swaps it for the tesla_id guard.
decisions.why: Dropping it in tier 1 leaves the write path with no authorization until tier 2. The delete handler proceeds on a lookup miss, so SQL is the only guard. main auto-deploys.

decisions.what: Database design confirmed: rename the column, drop idx_manual_charge_entries_account_time, replace the vehicle-time index with (tesla_id, charged_on DESC).
decisions.why: No row is deleted and no value rewritten, so Down is a true undo. Two indexes become one and it serves all four reads.

tiers.notes: Migration, queries and the four Reader ports. Leader-owned integration: the three internal/analytics call sites plus the mechanical internal/gateway call-site updates that keep the build green.
Update and Delete take a vehicleref.Ref. SQL guard becomes id AND tesla_id. Create is untouched and keeps the account for authorship.
The riskiest tier. Every manual-charge write proves the entry's own tesla_id with authorizeVehicle before touching a row.

events.detail: RM58 numbered from openspec/.work-counter (58 -> 59). Branch ft/RM58-MAG-68-rekey-manual-charges-on-tesla-id created off main. Budget at creation: five_hour_pct 11, context_pct 19.

MAG-68's description claimed internal/gateway was the only consumer. Verified false: internal/analytics calls three per-vehicle read ports. The Linear description was corrected before the roadmap was written.

MIGRATIONS_DIRS order account/telemetry/charging/analytics, one shared goose_db_version table; a 20260914 migration sorts after MAG-67's 20260912. make migration-guard passes, warning only about the pre-existing 20260720000001 collision (backlog item 21). sqlc risk recorded: per-query Row structs when a kept column stops being selected.

Owner confirmed the tier 1 database design. Owner also accepted the worker's D4 finding and chose to keep the account predicate in tier 1 (D5). Worker re-dispatched to revise the artifacts. Budget after artifact wave: five_hour_pct 47, context_pct 25.

Artifacts written and revised for D5. openspec validate --strict passes. Worker surfaced a user-visible consequence of D1+D5 combined: for tiers 1-2 a shared car's co-owner entries are listed with working-looking edit/delete controls, but the delete is a silent no-op because DeleteEntry is :exec and writerService.Delete never checks rows affected. Verified in code. Tier 3 removes the cause.
